summary:
Only fully pre-encoded supplier journal /4 and host-export-source journal /1 use PortableSourceJournalIO. The existing workspace/idempotency key, FileShare.None owner lock, source originals/fences, codecs and legacy write variants remain. The private Linux x64/arm64 path pins an O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor, binds the held managed lock to its directory entry using the documented statx identity fields, exclusively creates its private temporary name with openat, writes the complete bounded candidate, flushes the file, replaces within the same held directory, calls fsync on that same directory descriptor, then retains the lock for descriptor-relative exact/cold readback through the existing decoder. Unsupported native support refuses; there is no durability fallback.

The three additional fixed test cuts cover before directory sync, after sync before readback and a clearly simulated sync error; the five earlier cuts remain. Before replacement the previous bytes remain; later failure may have committed the new record and returns source commit uncertainty. An authenticated cold source read can recover the same original and consumed intent, not issue another attempt or replay an effect. Temporary-name cleanup assumes stable exclusive private-parent custody and preserves the primary exception. SafeFileHandle does not independently report underlying close errno; no observed-close success is claimed. A blocked fsync keeps its live owner/lock until syscall completion; managed timeout cannot release that custody.

The unchanged root initializer does not certify durable ancestry. Successful ordering is conditional on separately qualified pre-existing stateRoot/journal-v1, backing filesystem and namespace custody; it is not hardware/power-loss or arbitrary hostile-namespace protection. All public source results remain directory-durability Unknown, prepareAck and reserveHost remain refused, and no receiving authentication, production export/cleanup authority or host activation is supplied. The finite canonical model separates flush/replacement/sync/readback/response, permits old-or-new pre-sync crash recovery and blocked stuttering, and includes omitted-sync, premature-success and consumed-intent replay controls. It is separate from the Git-CAS GS20310JournalModel.

Dated root-accepted local SDK400 evidence on 2026-10-23 comprises genuine generation of nine compiled-output families and three raw Quint replay traces, 106 host/source controls, eight FsQuint replay tests and seven model tests. The original failures and actual private execution receipts remain outside Atlas; citations establish the source/contracts and do not alone prove that run. Source delivery, required CI, the separately owned401 focused preflight, frozen one-CPU/two-GiB payload fit, host-backed allocation/storage comparison, independent receiver commit and whole #4820/#4650 acceptance remain distinct.
title: Pinned-directory source journal synchronization preserves Unknown and consumed intent
